:::{#exm-kl-divergence-nonnegative}
#### Divergence of a biased coin from a fair coin

<!-- no-figure: the example is two numbers -->

Let $p = (0.9, 0.1)$ be the mass function of a biased coin, and let $q = (0.5, 0.5)$ be a fair coin.
The code below computes the divergence in each direction, in bits.

```{r}
#| label: kl-divergence-nonnegative
p <- c(0.9, 0.1)
q <- c(0.5, 0.5)
c(
  p_from_q = sum(p * log2(p / q)),
  q_from_p = sum(q * log2(q / p)),
  p_from_p = sum(p * log2(p / p))
)
```

Both divergences between the two coins are positive,
as @thm-kl-divergence-nonnegative requires,
and they differ, so the divergence is not symmetric.
The divergence of $p$ from itself is $0$.

:::
